map.subsystem: Alerting and notifications (GlycemicGPT Android — `domain/alerting`, `service/Alert*`, `data/local/AlertThresholdStore`, `data/repository/AlertRepository`, `presentation/alerts`, plus the wrist relay/coverage mirror)

capabilities.name: Alert type + severity vocabulary (server wire contract)
capabilities.behavior: `AlertTypes` object (domain/alerting/AlertTypes.kt) defines the ONLY alert-type vocabulary used for notification channel routing, notification slot derivation, and floor classification. Constants (exact strings, mirroring backend `models/alert.py`): LOW_URGENT="low_urgent", LOW_WARNING="low_warning", HIGH_WARNING="high_warning", HIGH_URGENT="high_urgent", IOB_WARNING="iob_warning". Derived sets: LOW_ALERT_TYPES = [low_urgent, low_warning] (route to the DND-bypassing alarm channel); HIGH_ALERT_TYPES = [high_warning, high_urgent]. `AlertSeverities`: WARNING="warning", URGENT="urgent", EMERGENCY="emergency". Additional server type observed at runtime but not in the object: "no_data" (caregiver data-gap alert, GLY-137) — it falls through channel routing to the AI channel. The watch wire protocol deliberately uses DIFFERENT strings (urgent_low/low/high/urgent_high); mapping only through `PumpPollingOrchestrator.SERVER_TO_WATCH_ALERT_TYPE`. A test (`classify never emits the watch vocabulary`) pins that the two vocabularies never mix.
edge_cases: Unknown/unmapped alert type routes to the AI (IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT, non-DND-bypassing) channel — a drifted low string is a silent safety downgrade, explicitly called out in the KDoc.
`SERVER_TO_WATCH_ALERT_TYPE` has no entry for iob_warning or no_data; a lookup miss logs a warning and yields null (relay push skipped) but must never abort the floor hand-off.

capabilities.name: Alert threshold storage (AlertThresholdStore)
capabilities.behavior: SharedPreferences file "alert_thresholds" (Context.MODE_PRIVATE). Four Int values in canonical mg/dL: urgentLow (key urgent_low, default 55), lowWarning (low_warning, 70), highWarning (high_warning, 180), urgentHigh (urgent_high, 250). Plus lastFetchedMs (last_fetched_ms, default 0) and source (key "source"). `ThresholdSource` enum: NONE (never configured — floor disarmed), BACKEND (synced from server; backend is master), LOCAL (user-set on device in BLE-only mode; survives logout). `source` getter: read persisted string and match an enum name; if absent, legacy fallback = BACKEND when lastFetchedMs != 0 else NONE (so pre-`source`-key installs stay armed across upgrade). `isConfigured()` = source != NONE — the floor's arming gate; defaults are NEVER alarmed off. `isConfiguredFlow()` is a callbackFlow that emits isConfigured() immediately then on every SharedPreferences change to KEY_SOURCE, KEY_LAST_FETCHED, or a null key (the null key covers `clear()`); unregisters the listener on close. `updateAll(ul,lw,hw,uh)` validates then writes all four + lastFetched=System.currentTimeMillis() + source=BACKEND in one `.commit()` (synchronous). `updateLocal(...)` validates then writes all four + source=LOCAL + lastFetched=0L explicitly (so a stale BACKEND timestamp can't survive under LOCAL values) via `.commit()`. Validation `requireSafeThresholds` (throws IllegalArgumentException, persisting NOTHING): (a) all four in 20..500 mg/dL — message "Alert thresholds out of the 20-500 mg/dL safety range"; (b) ordering urgentLow <= lowWarning < highWarning <= urgentHigh — note the OUTER comparisons are non-strict (rounded ties at urgent boundaries are legal) and the middle is strict. `clear()` wipes the whole prefs file ONLY when source == BACKEND; LOCAL values are deliberately preserved (they belong to the device, not the account). `isStale(maxAgeMs = STALE_THRESHOLD_MS)` = (now - lastFetchedMs) > maxAgeMs; STALE_THRESHOLD_MS = 3_600_000 ms (1 hour) — a never-synced (0) store is always stale.
edge_cases: `clear()` on a LOCAL store is a no-op — logout must not silently disarm a device-configured floor.
LOCAL source means isStale() is always true (lastFetchedMs=0); callers gate the refresh on backendConfigured before calling.
Defaults (55/70/180/250) exist ONLY so the watch alert relay's `classify()` has values; the floor never uses them because it gates on isConfigured().

capabilities.name: Backend threshold sync (server is master)
capabilities.behavior: `AuthRepository.fetchAlertThresholds()` GETs `/api/settings/alert-thresholds` → `AlertThresholdsResponse` (Floats: urgent_low, low_warning, high_warning, urgent_high, optional iob_warning which is IGNORED by the client). Validation runs on the RAW FLOATS for ordering (`urgentLow < lowWarning < highWarning < urgentHigh`, all strict) because rounding two server-legal values <1 mg/dL apart could collapse them to equal ints; values are then roundToInt() and range-checked `in 20..500`. If either check fails the whole response is DROPPED (logged "Alert thresholds invalid: %d/%d/%d/%d -- ignoring"), never clamped, leaving last-known-good values (or the never-synced disarmed state). On success `alertThresholdStore.updateAll(...)`; if the previous source was LOCAL, an audit log line records the backend takeover. Rounded ties (69.8/70.2 → 70/70) are explicitly safe because `classify` checks the urgent band first. Trigger points: (1) immediately after successful login (`scope.launch { fetchAlertThresholds() }`); (2) `refreshAlertThresholds()` from SettingsViewModel init when `alertThresholdStore.isStale()` and logged in; (3) HomeViewModel when backendConfigured && isStale(); (4) `refreshAlertThresholdsIfStale()` called on EVERY SSE heartbeat and on SSE open — heartbeats arrive ~every 30 s, and the 1-hour staleness window throttles this to at most one GET/hour, so web edits reach a never-opened pocket-monitor phone within an hour. `logout()` calls `alertThresholdStore.clear()` (BACKEND values wiped, floor disarmed) and `clearBaseUrl()` also calls `clear()` (going BLE-only must not leave server thresholds armed).
edge_cases: Non-2xx response body is silently ignored (no state change).
Any exception (except CancellationException, rethrown) is caught and logged; the cached values stand.
A valid backend fetch silently overwrites user-set LOCAL thresholds — backend is master (GLY-145).

capabilities.name: Local threshold editor (BLE-only mode, GLY-145)
capabilities.behavior: Settings → Notifications → "Alert Thresholds" card. When `backendConfigured` the section renders READ-ONLY: either "Urgent low X · Low Y · High Z · Urgent high W <unit>" or "Waiting for the first sync from your server.", plus "Edit alert thresholds in the GlycemicGPT web app; they sync to this phone automatically." When NOT backendConfigured the user edits four decimal-keyboard fields (Urgent low / Low / High / Urgent high) and taps "Save Thresholds". Status line above the fields: "On-device alarms are armed at these levels." (configured) or "On-device alarms are OFF until you set all four thresholds." in error color (unconfigured). `SettingsViewModel.saveLocalAlertThresholds(4 strings)`: (1) live re-check `authRepository.isBackendConfigured()` — no-op if a server URL was saved earlier in the same Settings session; (2) parse each field in the user's DISPLAY unit via `parseThresholdMgDl` (trim, replace ',' with '.', toDoubleOrNull, reject non-finite; mg/dL → roundToInt, mmol/L → (value * 18.0156).roundToInt()); null on any field → error "Enter a number for all four thresholds."; (3) range check `in 20..500` → "Thresholds must be between <bounds> ." where the bounds label is unit-aware — for mmol it is the outermost 0.1-step values that round back INTO 20..500: min = ceil((20-0.5)*10/18.0156)/10, max = floor((500+0.499)*10/18.0156)/10 (naive 500/18.0156=27.8 would round to 501 and be rejected by its own message); (4) ordering check `ul <= lw && lw < hw && hw <= uh` → "Thresholds must increase: urgent low ≤ low < high ≤ urgent high."; (5) `alertThresholdStore.updateLocal(...)` and UI state update. `clearAlertThresholdError()` clears the inline error on the next keystroke. Store-level `require()` remains as defense-in-depth.
edge_cases: Editing in mmol/L round-trips through mg/dL; the displayed values re-derive from the stored mg/dL, so a saved 3.9 mmol renders back as 3.9 (70 mg/dL).
Fields are keyed on `remember(storedValue, unit)` so a unit switch re-seeds them.
Saving is blocked (silent no-op) the instant a backend URL exists.

capabilities.name: SSE alert stream service (AlertStreamService)
capabilities.behavior: Foreground Service (`foregroundServiceType="dataSync"`, not exported), NOTIFICATION_ID = 2, CHANNEL_ID = "alert_stream", channel name "Alert Monitoring", IMPORTANCE_LOW, setShowBadge(false), description "Monitors for glucose alerts from the server". Foreground notification: title "GlycemicGPT Alert Monitor", text "Listening for glucose alerts", ongoing, silent. Returns START_STICKY. Endpoint: GET `<baseUrl>/api/v1/alerts/stream` with headers `Authorization: Bearer <rawToken>` and `Accept: text/event-stream`, via OkHttp `EventSources.createFactory(sseClient).newEventSource(...)`. Dedicated OkHttpClient (lazily built, reused across reconnects): connectTimeout 30 s, readTimeout 75 s (server heartbeats every 30 s; 75 s = 2.5 intervals — tolerates one fully missed heartbeat plus jitter and bounds how long a silently dead stream can look CONNECTED, i.e. the worst-case delay before the degraded banner appears), plus the debug `SimulateUnreachableInterceptor`. Events handled: type "alert" → `handleAlertEvent` (Moshi `AlertResponse` adapter); type "heartbeat" → verbose log + `authRepository.refreshAlertThresholdsIfStale()`. Every `onEvent` calls `resetBackoffIfStable()`: resets reconnectAttempt to 0 only if connectionOpenedAtMs > 0 and now - connectionOpenedAtMs >= STABLE_CONNECTION_MS = 10_000 ms (prevents rapid connect/fail cycles from pinning backoff at 0). `onOpen` (guarded by generation): state → CONNECTED, connectionOpenedAtMs = now, and launches `alertRepository.reconcilePendingAcks()` (the SSE client bypasses ReachabilityInterceptor so NetworkMonitor may never emit the REACHABLE transition on a stream-only phone). `onFailure`: generation-guarded; if HTTP 401/403, `reconnectAttempt.set(max(5, attempt))` (longer backoff); state → RECONNECTING; scheduleReconnect(). `onClosed`: generation-guarded; state → RECONNECTING; scheduleReconnect(). Reconnect backoff: `min(1000L * (1 shl attempt.coerceAtMost(6)), MAX_BACKOFF_MS=60_000)` → 1 s, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 60 (capped) s; a single-flight `AtomicBoolean reconnectScheduled` CAS prevents overlapping schedules; `reconnectAttempt.incrementAndGet()` happens synchronously at schedule time. After the delay: if state is already CONNECTED, skip (another path healed it); else if `authTokenStore.hasActiveSession()` reconnect, otherwise state → DISCONNECTED and `stopSelf()`. Concurrency: `@Volatile eventSource`, `@Volatile destroyed`, `AtomicInteger connectionGeneration` — stale callbacks whose generation != the captured `gen` are dropped; `connectToStream()` and `shutDownStream()` are both `@Synchronized`. `onStartCommand` is idempotent: it skips reconnecting when eventSource != null AND state == CONNECTED, so a redundant start (Settings open, re-login) does not flash "server alerts paused". `onDestroy`: shutDownStream (destroyed=true, generation bump BEFORE cancel, eventSource.cancel(), state → DISCONNECTED), cancel reconnect job, `dispatcher.executorService.shutdownNow()` + awaitTermination(3 s), connectionPool.evictAll(), cancel serviceScope. Debug-only: collects `simulateBackendUnreachableFlow()` and force-cancels the live eventSource when the toggle flips on (an already-open stream would otherwise sit CONNECTED for up to the 75 s read timeout).
edge_cases: Missing base URL or missing raw token → log + state DISCONNECTED, no connection attempt.
`connectToStream()` increments `connectionGeneration` twice (once before cancelling the previous source, once when capturing `gen`); harmless but note it if porting the guard verbatim.
401/403 does not trigger a token refresh here — it only lengthens the backoff; recovery depends on AuthManager refreshing elsewhere.

Started from: successful login (AuthRepository.login), SettingsViewModel init when logged in, BootCompletedReceiver when a refresh token exists. Stopped from: AuthRepository.logout, and self-stop when no active session at reconnect time.

capabilities.name: Alert stream state machine (AlertStreamStateHolder)
capabilities.behavior: `enum AlertStreamState { CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED, RECONNECTING }` held in a @Singleton MutableStateFlow, initial value DISCONNECTED. Transitions driven exclusively by AlertStreamService: `onStreamOpened()` → CONNECTED (SSE onOpen); `onStreamRetrying()` → RECONNECTING (onFailure/onClosed, reconnect scheduled); `onStreamStopped()` → DISCONNECTED (service destroyed, no session, no base URL/token, shutDownStream). Anything other than CONNECTED means no new server alerts arrive, and is half of the alert floor's arm-condition. ViewModels/services collect `state`; the Service is the sole writer (a seam because ViewModels cannot observe an Android Service).
edge_cases: State is process-scoped, not persisted: a cold start reads DISCONNECTED, which is the pessimistic (degraded) value — deliberate fail-closed.

capabilities.name: Server alert ingestion and persistence
capabilities.behavior: `AlertResponse` (Moshi): id, alert_type, severity, current_value (Double), predicted_value?, iob_value?, message, trend_rate?, timestamp (ISO-8601 string), patient_name?, acknowledged (default false). `AlertRepository.saveAlert(response)` parses `Instant.parse(timestamp).toEpochMilli()`, falling back to `System.currentTimeMillis()` on any parse failure, then calls `AlertDao.insertPreservingLocalAck(entity)` with ackSynced = response.acknowledged. Room entity `alerts` (AlertEntity): autoGenerate id PK, server_id (unique index), alert_type, severity, message, current_value REAL, predicted_value?, iob_value?, trend_rate?, patient_name?, acknowledged (Bool, LOCAL/user-intent truth), ack_synced (Bool, defaultValue "0"), timestamp_ms (indexed); also an index on acknowledged. `insertPreservingLocalAck` is a @Transaction: read existing by server_id; if existing != null && existing.acknowledged && !incoming.acknowledged → merge to `acknowledged=true, ackSynced=existing.ackSynced` (GLY-130 clobber guard: an SSE re-delivery or pull must never downgrade a local ack and re-fire the alarm); REPLACE-insert the merged row and RETURN it. Callers MUST branch on the returned entity's `acknowledged`, not on the raw response. `observeRecentAlerts()` = `SELECT * FROM alerts ORDER BY timestamp_ms DESC LIMIT 100` as a Flow. `fetchPendingAlerts()` (GET /api/v1/alerts/pending) FIRST calls reconcilePendingAcks() (so the pull cannot resurrect an alert acked offline), then saves each returned alert; non-2xx throws RuntimeException("Fetch alerts failed: HTTP <code>"). `cleanupOldAlerts(maxAgeDays = 7)` deletes rows with timestamp_ms < now - 7 days; called from AlertsViewModel.init.
edge_cases: A malformed/absent ISO timestamp silently becomes "now" — the alert still shows but its age is wrong.
Floor alerts are NEVER written to this table (it is server history only); their synthetic serverId carries the `local-floor:` prefix.
The alerts table is not touched by DataRetentionWorker (that worker only prunes pump readings); the only prune is cleanupOldAlerts on Alerts-screen open.

capabilities.name: Notification channels, sounds, and versioning
capabilities.behavior: Three alert channels, all created in `AlertNotificationManager.init` (and re-created on sound change), with VERSIONED ids because an Android channel's sound is immutable after creation: `low_alerts_v<n>`, `high_alerts_v<n>`, `ai_notifications_v<n>` (version default 1, stored per-category in SharedPreferences "alert_sounds"). LOW channel: name "Low Glucose Alerts", IMPORTANCE_HIGH, description "Life-threatening low glucose alerts", setBypassDnd(true), enableVibration(true), vibrationPattern longArrayOf(0, 500, 200, 500, 200, 500), sound = user URI or RingtoneManager default TYPE_ALARM with AudioAttributes USAGE_ALARM / CONTENT_TYPE_SONIFICATION. HIGH channel: "High Glucose Alerts", IMPORTANCE_HIGH, "High glucose and insulin alerts", setBypassDnd(true), enableVibration(true) (no custom pattern), sound = user URI or default TYPE_NOTIFICATION with USAGE_NOTIFICATION_EVENT / CONTENT_TYPE_SONIFICATION. AI channel: "AI Notifications", IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT, "AI analysis insights and daily briefs", no DND bypass, sound = user URI or default TYPE_NOTIFICATION with USAGE_NOTIFICATION / CONTENT_TYPE_SONIFICATION, or setSound(null,null) when the stored URI is the SILENT sentinel. Legacy channels deleted on init: urgent_alerts, standard_alerts, urgent_alerts_v2, standard_alerts_v2. `recreateChannel(category)` (under `channelLock`): delete old versioned channel, `incrementChannelVersion` (non-atomic read-modify-write — caller MUST hold channelLock), re-create with the new version and current sound. `AlertSoundStore` (prefs file "alert_sounds") keys: low/high/ai sound URI, low/high/ai display name, `override_silent_for_low` (Boolean, default TRUE), low/high/ai channel version (Int, default 1). SILENT_URI sentinel = "silent" (distinguished from null = "use system default"); only the AI category exposes a Silent option in the picker. Sound selection (SettingsViewModel.onSoundSelected) validates the URI by constructing a Ringtone (falls back to default name on failure), takes a persistable read URI permission (SecurityException swallowed), stores URI+name, then calls recreateChannel. Channel resolution (`resolveChannelIdLocked`): alertType in LOW_ALERT_TYPES → low channel; in HIGH_ALERT_TYPES → high channel; everything else (iob_warning, no_data, unknown) → AI channel.
edge_cases: Channel version bumps are permanent and monotonic; the old channel is deleted so user-customised settings on it are lost — accepted cost of changing the sound.
The AI sound picker row is HIDDEN in BLE-only mode (GLY-146) since that channel can never fire without a backend.
Posting happens under the same `channelLock` as recreation so a channel cannot be deleted between resolve and notify.

capabilities.name: Alert notification rendering and actions
capabilities.behavior: `showAlertNotification(alert: AlertEntity, notificationId: Int)`. Guard: returns immediately (logged) if `canPostAlertNotifications()` is false. If the alert is a LOW type AND `alertSoundStore.overrideSilentForLowAlerts` is true → `boostAlarmVolume()`. Built with NotificationCompat: smallIcon android.R.drawable.ic_dialog_alert; contentTitle = `formatAlertTitle(alert, appSettingsStore.glucoseUnit)`; contentText = alert.message with BigTextStyle bigText(message); priority = PRIORITY_HIGH when severity in {"urgent","emergency"} else PRIORITY_DEFAULT; contentIntent = Activity PendingIntent to MainActivity with FLAG_ACTIVITY_SINGLE_TOP|FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TOP and extra `navigate_to="alerts"` (request code = serverId.hashCode(), FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT|FLAG_IMMUTABLE); setAutoCancel(true); setGroup("com.glycemicgpt.ALERTS"); `setOnlyAlertOnce(!isLow)` — lows re-fire sound on every update because they are life-threatening, highs/IoB alert once then update silently; `setLocalOnly(isLocalOnlyOnWrist(alert))`; one action: icon ic_menu_close_clear_cancel, label "Got It", Broadcast PendingIntent to AlertActionReceiver with action ACTION_ACKNOWLEDGE and extras EXTRA_SERVER_ID / EXTRA_NOTIFICATION_ID (request code = serverId.hashCode() xor "ack".hashCode(), deliberately distinct from the content intent's). Title format (`formatAlertTitle`, pure): prefix by severity — "EMERGENCY"/"URGENT"/"Warning"/"Info" (else branch); patientSuffix = " - <patientName>" when present; if alertType == "no_data" the title is "<prefix>: No CGM data<suffix>" (a data-gap alert's currentValue is only a LAST-KNOWN reading — rendering it would fake a live value during the very blackout being reported); otherwise "<prefix>: <GlucoseFormat.formatWithLabel(currentValue.toInt(), unit)><suffix>" e.g. "EMERGENCY: 320 mg/dL - Alice" / "EMERGENCY: 17.8 mmol/L". `isLocalOnlyOnWrist(alert)` = serverId.startsWith("local-floor:") — device-computed floor notifications must NOT bridge to a paired watch (the data-layer relay already covers exactly those fires; bridging would double-buzz); SERVER alerts must keep bridging because they fire off a different (cloud) glucose source and are the only wrist path while the pump CGM is stale.
edge_cases: `navigate_to="alerts"` is a DEAD extra: MainActivity has no onNewIntent/getIntent handling at all (the manifest comment explicitly states no incoming intent extras are processed), so tapping a notification just opens the app at its normal start destination. Deep-linking to the Alerts tab is NOT implemented today.
Alert values are rendered in the user's display unit; the stored currentValue stays canonical mg/dL.
Severity strings are compared as raw literals here ("urgent", "emergency") rather than via AlertSeverities.

capabilities.name: Notification slot (stable ID) and per-server-ID dedup
capabilities.behavior: `stableNotificationId(alert)`: key = "${alert.alertType}|${alert.patientName ?: ""}"; id = (key.hashCode() and 0x7FFFFFFF).coerceAtLeast(100) — always positive and above the foreground-service IDs (1 = PumpConnection, 2 = AlertStream). Same type (and same patient, for caregivers) share a slot so Android REPLACES rather than stacks; this is also what makes a server re-delivery on reconnect replace an on-device floor notification instead of duplicating it. serverId is deliberately ignored. Separate dedup layer `shouldNotify(serverId)`: a LinkedHashSet `notifiedServerIds` guarded by `dedupLock`; returns true only the first time a serverId is seen; when the set exceeds MAX_NOTIFIED_IDS = 200 the oldest entries are evicted (insertion-order iterator) down to 200. `markAcknowledged(serverId)` removes the id so a later re-issue can notify again. The set is process-scoped (survives SSE reconnects, not process death).
edge_cases: Hash collisions across different type|patient keys would merge two slots — accepted.

Process restart clears notifiedServerIds; a re-delivered still-unacked alert would notify again (but the Room `acknowledged` guard in AlertStreamService.handleAlertEvent prevents re-alarming an acked one).

capabilities.name: Alarm volume boost and restore
capabilities.behavior: Supplementary loudness for low alerts, FreeStyle-Libre style, gated on `AlertSoundStore.overrideSilentForLowAlerts` (default true; Settings toggle "Boost Volume for Lows" with copy noting low/high alerts always bypass DND regardless). `boostAlarmVolume()`: read STREAM_ALARM current and max; if current < max, persist current as savedAlarmVolume then setStreamVolume(STREAM_ALARM, max, 0). savedAlarmVolume is persisted in SharedPreferences "alert_volume" (key "saved_alarm_volume", -1 = no boost active) so it survives process death. `restoreAlarmVolume()`: no-op if saved < 0; otherwise setStreamVolume(STREAM_ALARM, saved, 0) and only THEN clear to -1 (so a failed restore is retried later); failures are caught and logged. Restore is invoked from `AlertNotificationManager.init` (recovering a boost left behind by a process restart) and from `AlertActionReceiver.handleAcknowledge` on every ack.
edge_cases: If a second low fires while a boost is already active, current == max so no new save happens — the original pre-boost level is preserved.
Requires MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS; exceptions are swallowed with a warning.

capabilities.name: Acknowledge ("Got It") flow — AlertActionReceiver
capabilities.behavior: BroadcastReceiver (not exported), ACTION_ACKNOWLEDGE = "com.glycemicgpt.mobile.ACTION_ACKNOWLEDGE_ALERT", extras "extra_server_id" and "extra_notification_id". `onReceive` ignores other actions, requires the server-id extra, reads notificationId (default -1), calls `goAsync()` and runs on `GlobalScope.launch(Dispatchers.IO)` (deliberate: the receiver instance may be GC'd; the coroutine is tied only to the pendingResult, finished in a `finally`). `handleAcknowledge(serverId, notificationId)` — the ORDER is a pinned safety invariant (GLY-130, `coVerifyOrder` test): (1) `alertRepository.markAcknowledgedLocally(serverId)` — a local-only Room write first, so an SSE re-delivery landing mid-silence hits the acknowledged-row guard instead of re-alarming; (2) if notificationId >= 0, `cancelNotification(notificationId)`; (3) `restoreAlarmVolume()`; (4) `markAcknowledged(serverId)` (clears the dedup id); ALL unconditional and network-independent — an unreachable backend can never leave the alarm sounding. (5) If serverId starts with "local-floor:": parse the type via `floorAlertTypeFromServerId` and call `alertFloor.onFloorAlertAcknowledged(type)`, then RETURN — a synthetic id must never reach the server acknowledge endpoint. (6) Otherwise `alertRepository.acknowledgeAlert(serverId)`; success/failure are only logged (failure is deferred to reconcile), never allowed to un-silence. `floorAlertTypeFromServerId(serverId)` = removePrefix("local-floor:").substringBeforeLast(':', missingDelimiterValue = "").ifEmpty { null } → "local-floor:low_urgent:175000" → "low_urgent"; "local-floor:" → null; "local-floor:oops" → null.
edge_cases: notificationId == -1 (missing extra) skips only the cancel; every other silence op still runs.
A server-alert ack never touches the floor cooldown, and a floor ack never POSTs — both pinned by test.

capabilities.name: Acknowledge sync, terminal-vs-transient classification, and reconcile
capabilities.behavior: `AlertRepository.acknowledgeAlert(serverId)` inside runCatching: mark the Room row `acknowledged=1, ack_synced=0` FIRST (unconditional), then POST `/api/v1/alerts/{alertId}/acknowledge`. Outcome classification (`ackOutcomeOf`, shared by both ack paths): 2xx → SYNCED (mark ack_synced=1); code in TERMINAL_ACK_CODES = {403, 404, 422} → TERMINAL (mark ack_synced=1 to stop the reconcile retrying forever, but still throw `AlertAckHttpException(code, terminal=true)` so the caller can surface a real error); anything else (transport failure, 5xx, 401 before a refresh) → TRANSIENT (row stays pending, throw `AlertAckHttpException(code, terminal=false)`). CancellationException is rethrown from the onFailure hook so scope cancellation stays cooperative. `reconcilePendingAcks()` — never throws, safe to call opportunistically (endpoint is idempotent), serialized by a `reconcileMutex`: reads `getPendingAckServerIds()` (`acknowledged=1 AND ack_synced=0 ORDER BY timestamp_ms ASC, id ASC`); returns early if empty; per row, SYNCED or TERMINAL stamps ack_synced=1, TRANSIENT logs and leaves pending; an IOException ABORTS the whole pass (the backend is still unreachable so the remaining POSTs would fail identically) leaving the rest pending; any other unexpected exception logs and continues to the next row. Reconcile triggers (exactly three): (a) every emission of `NetworkMonitor.status` equal to REACHABLE, collected app-wide in `GlycemicGptApp.onCreate` — including the initial value on cold start, which is what drains acks pending across process death; (b) SSE `onOpen`; (c) the head of `fetchPendingAlerts()`.
edge_cases: 401 is classified TRANSIENT on purpose — a token refresh may fix it.
A terminal rejection still leaves the alert dismissed on this device; only the server copy diverges.

Because `markAcknowledgedPending` is a bare UPDATE, acking a serverId with no Room row (e.g. a floor alert) is a silent no-op — that is why the floor path relies on its own in-memory cooldown state instead.

capabilities.name: On-device alert floor — arming gates and firing (AlertFloor, GLY-115)
capabilities.behavior: @Singleton. THE safety invariant: never fire on a non-FRESH reading. Threshold-only by design — NO trajectory projection, NO prediction horizons, NO IoB escalation (those stay server-side; the disclaimer text says so). `classify(mgDl): String?` in the SERVER vocabulary, urgent bands first: mgDl <= urgentLowMgDl → low_urgent; mgDl >= urgentHighMgDl → high_urgent; mgDl <= lowWarningMgDl → low_warning; mgDl >= highWarningMgDl → high_warning; else null (in range). Boundaries are inclusive at both urgent and warning edges (55→low_urgent, 56→low_warning, 70→low_warning, 71→null, 179→null, 180→high_warning, 249→high_warning, 250→high_urgent). `onCgmReading(reading, alertType, nowMs = now)` executes in this order: (0) wall-clock rewind guard — if `isWallClockRewound(nowMs)` log and RETURN (recovery handling is skipped too, since an understated age could fake a recovery); else `noteWallClock(nowMs)`. (1) Episode recovery: under `fireMutex`, every ACKED type that is not the current alertType is fully re-armed (removed from ackedTypes and from lastFiredAtMsByType) — a re-cross is a distinct episode and alarms immediately. UNACKED cooldowns deliberately survive boundary flapping. (2) if alertType == null return. (3) Gate 1 — arm only while server alerting is degraded: `if (!isAlertingDegraded(networkMonitor.status.value, alertStreamStateHolder.state.value)) return`. (4) Gates 2+3 via `isReadingAlertable(reading, nowMs)` (freshness + thresholds-configured + rewind); on failure log which of the two failed and return. (5) Gate 4 — `alertNotificationManager.canPostAlertNotifications()`; checked BEFORE the cooldown is stamped so a permission granted a minute later does not find the alarm already spent. (6) Under `fireMutex`: if lastFiredAtMsByType[type] exists and nowMs - it < FLOOR_COOLDOWN_MS → return. (7) Episode guard: `alertDao.getLatestUnacknowledgedTimestampForType(alertType, nowMs - FLOOR_COOLDOWN_MS)` (SQL: MAX(timestamp_ms) WHERE alert_type=? AND acknowledged=0 AND timestamp_ms >= ?); a DB exception is caught and treated as null — FAIL TOWARD ALERTING (a broken lookup may cost a duplicate alarm, never a missed one). If non-null, seed lastFiredAtMsByType[type] = min(recentServerAlertMs, nowMs) (clamped so a server clock ahead of the phone cannot stretch the window past 30 min) and return without firing. (8) Fire: build the floor AlertEntity, `showAlertNotification(entity, stableNotificationId(entity))`, stamp lastFiredAtMsByType[type] = nowMs, remove type from ackedTypes, log. Constant: FLOOR_COOLDOWN_MS = 30 * 60_000 = 1_800_000 ms, mirroring the server's DEDUP_WINDOW_MINUTES = 30. Floor entity: serverId = "local-floor:<alertType>:<reading.timestamp epochMs>"; alertType = server vocabulary; severity = "urgent" for low_urgent/high_urgent else "warning"; currentValue = glucoseMgDl.toDouble(); timestampMs = reading sensor timestamp; message = "<headline> <value+unit> — computed on your phone from your last sensor reading. Threshold-only, no prediction. Not a replacement for your CGM app." where headline ∈ {"Urgent low glucose", "Low glucose", "High glucose", "Urgent high glucose", fallback "Glucose alert"}. The entity is NEVER persisted to Room.
edge_cases: Evaluation happens ONLY on a newly polled (or debug-injected) CGM reading — with the pump link down the floor cannot fire at all no matter how fresh the cached reading looks (this is the implicit fifth gate mirrored as PUMP_DISCONNECTED in the status).
No shared UUIDs with the server exist, so dedup is layered: gate 1 (source), shared notification slot (replace not stack), per-type cooldown, and the ack-gated episode guard.
The floor alarms in the server AlertType vocabulary specifically so the notification slot and channel routing match a server re-delivery.

capabilities.name: Alert floor — shared data-trust bound (isReadingAlertable)
capabilities.behavior: `isReadingAlertable(reading, nowMs = now): Boolean` is the SINGLE bound shared by every consumer that may alert a human off a local pump CGM reading (GLY-116 D2): (1) if `isWallClockRewound(nowMs)` return false; (2) `noteWallClock(nowMs)` — deliberately NOT pure: every caller advances the monotonic high-water mark, which can only make rewind detection more aggressive; (3) if `!alertThresholdStore.isConfigured()` return false; (4) return `isFreshForAlertFloor(nowMs - reading.timestamp.toEpochMilli(), FreshnessPolicy.cgm(appSettingsStore.debugFastStaleness))`. Both the floor's firing path AND the watch relay (`PumpPollingOrchestrator.processCgmReading`) call THIS function — a second staleness definition on either path is the silent-floor bug GLY-115/116 exist to prevent (pinned by `AlertRelayFloorDivergenceTest` and `AlertFloorArmingConsistencyTest`). Deliberately NOT part of the bound: degraded-state, notification permission, cooldowns — those are floor-firing concerns wrapped around the predicate (a stale reading must not alert the wrist whether the backend is up or down).
edge_cases: Age is computed against the CGM's OWN sensor timestamp, never poll wall-clock — a warmup or signal-loss poll can succeed every 15 s while returning the same old sensor value.

capabilities.name: Alert floor — wall-clock rewind guard
capabilities.behavior: `@Volatile wallClockHighWaterMs` (init 0). `noteWallClock(nowMs)` raises it monotonically (plain @Volatile is sufficient: a lost racing update can only lower the mark slightly, never raise it wrongly). `isWallClockRewound(nowMs)` = `nowMs + ALERT_FLOOR_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS < wallClockHighWaterMs`, i.e. now runs more than 60 s behind the highest wall-clock time ever observed. While true: the floor suppresses evaluation entirely AND the status surface treats the CGM age as absent (→ NOT watching). The mark is fed by every floor evaluation, every isReadingAlertable call (floor and relay alike), and every AlertFloorStatusProvider tick, so it stays current even with no CGM flowing. Documented residual, accepted: a rewind larger than the tolerance occurring while the process is NOT running leaves no water mark, so a stale reading can under-age by the rewind amount — a rare OVER-alarm edge that fails toward alarming, never toward silence.
edge_cases: A 30 s backward NTP nudge (within the 60 s tolerance) is NOT treated as a rewind — over-suppressing on routine drift would silently disable the floor, the same lethal failure inverted.
The mark is process-scoped; it is not persisted.

capabilities.name: Alert floor — acknowledge / bounded-snooze episode semantics
capabilities.behavior: `onFloorAlertAcknowledged(alertType, nowMs = now)` (suspend, under fireMutex): sets lastFiredAtMsByType[alertType] = nowMs and adds the type to `ackedTypes`. Semantics — an ack means "seen", never "snooze forever" and never "re-alarm every poll": (a) the ongoing episode is silenced and the 30-minute cooldown RESTARTS from the ack; (b) any subsequently evaluated reading that no longer classifies as that type fully re-arms it (removed from both maps), so a re-cross alarms IMMEDIATELY as a distinct episode even well inside the raw 30-minute window; (c) a sustained low that never recovers re-alarms exactly FLOOR_COOLDOWN_MS (30 min) after the ack — the floor can never go permanently silent on an ongoing emergency. Documented DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from the server, which re-alerts an acked sustained low on its own evaluation cadence: re-alarming every 15 s poll would be alarm-spam that trains users to disable notifications. Ack of one type never clears another type's cooldown. Unacknowledged cooldowns do NOT re-arm on recovery (boundary flapping of a hovering glucose must not re-alarm while the notification is still up).
edge_cases: ackedTypes/lastFiredAtMsByType are in-memory only — a process restart re-arms everything (the episode guard against Room server history is the only cross-process dedup, and it does not cover floor-only fires).

capabilities.name: Freshness policy and the alert-floor freshness gate
capabilities.behavior: `enum Freshness { FRESH, STALE, TOO_STALE }`. `FreshnessThresholds(staleAfterMs, tooStaleAfterMs)` with an init require(staleAfterMs in 1 until tooStaleAfterMs); half-open classification: age < staleAfterMs → FRESH; age < tooStaleAfterMs → STALE; else TOO_STALE (so exactly-at-boundary is the LATER tier). Negative ages classify as FRESH (correct for display). `FreshnessPolicy.CGM = (staleAfterMs = 6 min = 360_000, tooStaleAfterMs = 15 min = 900_000)` — one missed ~5-min sensor reading is STALE, three is TOO_STALE. `FreshnessPolicy.PUMP = (15 min = 900_000, 60 min = 3_600_000)` for IOB/basal/battery/reservoir. `FreshnessPolicy.CGM_DEBUG_FAST = (20_000, 45_000)` — debug-only compressed policy, substituted ONLY when the "Fast staleness" fault-injection toggle is on. `FreshnessPolicy.cgm(debugFastStaleness)` is the single swap point. `ALERT_FLOOR_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS = 60_000`. `isFreshForAlertFloor(ageMs, thresholds)` = `ageMs >= -60_000 && thresholds.classify(max(ageMs,0)) == FRESH` — strictly FRESH (STALE and TOO_STALE both fail), with an explicit forward-skew guard because pump and phone clocks routinely drift by seconds and a hard `age >= 0` would silently disable the floor. `relativeAgeLabel(ageMs)`: <60 s "just now", <3600 s "Xm ago", <86_400 s "Xh ago", else "Xd ago".
edge_cases: Boundary pairs pinned by test: age 359_999 ms alertable, 360_000 ms not; age -60_000 alertable, -60_001 not; under CGM_DEBUG_FAST 19_999 alertable, 20_000 not.
The wear module mirrors these numbers independently in `WatchFreshness` (6/15/60 min, 60 s skew) because it cannot depend on `:app` — drift between the two is a documented risk.

capabilities.name: Alerting-degraded predicate and alert-floor status (honest coverage claim)
capabilities.behavior: `isAlertingDegraded(networkStatus, streamState)` = `networkStatus != REACHABLE || streamState != CONNECTED` — deliberately pessimistic on disagreement (the SSE read timeout is 75 s so NetworkStatus usually notices an outage first; conversely a stream stuck reconnecting is degraded even while HTTP works). `enum FloorNotWatchingReason { NOTIFICATIONS_DENIED, THRESHOLDS_NOT_SYNCED, THRESHOLDS_NOT_CONFIGURED, PUMP_DISCONNECTED, NO_FRESH_READING }` — ORDERED by how actionable the cause is; when several fail at once the most actionable one wins. `sealed interface AlertFloorStatus { ServerActive; FloorWatching; FloorNotWatching(reason) }`. Pure selector `alertFloorStatus(networkStatus, streamState, cgmAgeMs, cgmThresholds, thresholdsConfigured, backendConfigured, canNotify, pumpConnected)` evaluated strictly in this order: (1) !isAlertingDegraded → ServerActive; (2) !canNotify → NOTIFICATIONS_DENIED; (3) !thresholdsConfigured → THRESHOLDS_NOT_SYNCED if backendConfigured else THRESHOLDS_NOT_CONFIGURED; (4) !pumpConnected → PUMP_DISCONNECTED; (5) cgmAgeMs != null && isFreshForAlertFloor(cgmAgeMs, cgmThresholds) → FloorWatching; (6) else NO_FRESH_READING. `backendConfigured` only ever selects the missing-thresholds REASON — it must never widen or narrow the coverage claim (pinned by a test grid). Every input the floor's firing path gates on is mirrored here, plus pumpConnected (the floor's implicit fifth gate).
edge_cases: The claim can never say more than the floor can deliver — claiming coverage while the floor cannot fire is described as "the lethal lie" the design exists to prevent.
cgmAgeMs is passed as null while the wall clock is rewound, collapsing to NO_FRESH_READING.

capabilities.name: AlertFloorStatusProvider — the single observation pipeline
capabilities.behavior: @Singleton producing a cold `Flow<AlertFloorStatus>` shared by the in-app banner, the pump foreground-notification text, and the wrist status forwarder (one pipeline so the three claims can never disagree). Structure: outer `combine(appSettingsStore.debugFastStalenessFlow(), authTokenStore.backendConfiguredFlow(), alertThresholdStore.isConfiguredFlow())` → distinctUntilChanged → flatMapLatest; inside, thresholds = FreshnessPolicy.cgm(fast) and tickMs = `(thresholds.staleAfterMs / 4).coerceIn(MIN_TICK_MS = 2_000, MAX_TICK_MS = 30_000)` → 30 s for the real CGM policy (360_000/4 = 90_000 clamped to 30_000), 5 s under the debug-fast policy; then `combine(networkMonitor.status, alertStreamStateHolder.state, pumpDataRepository.observeLatestCgm(), pumpConnectionManager.connectionState, tickerFlow(tickMs))`. On each emission: nowMs = System.currentTimeMillis(); `alertFloor.noteWallClock(nowMs)`; cgmAgeMs = null when `alertFloor.isWallClockRewound(nowMs)` else nowMs - cgm.timestamp; then `alertFloorStatus(...)` with canNotify = `alertNotificationManager.canPostAlertNotifications()` and pumpConnected = (pumpState == ConnectionState.CONNECTED). Recomputing on a ticker is essential because the decisive input (reading age) grows with no new emissions — the "watching" claim must DECAY to "NOT watching" on its own. `.retryWhen { ... }`: on any upstream failure it logs, `emit(current())` (a pessimistic snapshot — the claim degrades, it never lies or stops), delays RETRY_DELAY_MS = 5_000, and resubscribes. Terminal `.distinctUntilChanged()`. `current()` is the synchronous pessimistic seed: same selector with cgmAgeMs = null (Room read is async) and backendConfigured = false (avoids a main-thread encrypted-store decrypt; only affects the reason copy for the first frame) — a safety surface may briefly under-claim but must never default to a healthy state it cannot vouch for.
edge_cases: Threshold configuration is REACTIVE (isConfiguredFlow) rather than sampled per tick, so a Settings save arms the claim immediately and a logout disarm drops it immediately.
Each collector gets its own ticker (cold flow).

capabilities.name: Degraded banner copy (two modes, GLY-145)
capabilities.behavior: Pure `alertingDegradedBannerText(status, backendConfigured): String?`. ServerActive → null (no banner; the early return is the single owner of the visibility rule). FloorWatching, backend mode → "Server alerts paused — this phone is watching your latest sensor reading and will alarm for lows and highs. Threshold-only, no prediction. Alerts below are from before the disconnect."; BLE-only → "This phone is watching your latest sensor reading and will alarm for lows and highs. Threshold-only, no prediction." FloorNotWatching always leads with "Monitoring degraded — this phone is NOT watching for lows or highs: " then a reason tail: NOTIFICATIONS_DENIED → "notifications are disabled for GlycemicGPT. Enable notifications to restore on-phone alarms."; THRESHOLDS_NOT_SYNCED → "alert thresholds haven't synced from your server yet." when backendConfigured, otherwise the Settings line (the reason and the flag arrive on separate flows, so the copy re-checks rather than asserting a server that is gone); THRESHOLDS_NOT_CONFIGURED → "set your alert thresholds in Settings to turn on alarms."; PUMP_DISCONNECTED → "no pump connection, so no new readings are arriving."; NO_FRESH_READING → "no recent glucose reading."; then, only when backendConfigured, the suffix " No new alerts will arrive until the connection is restored." Rendered by `AlertingDegradedBanner` — a Surface with errorContainer color, 8dp rounded corners, CloudOff icon (20dp), 12dp padding, bodySmall Medium text in onErrorContainer; testTag "alerting_degraded_banner". Shown at the top of the Alerts screen only (not on Home).
edge_cases: Tests pin that NO BLE-only copy variant ever mentions a server or a restorable connection, and that every NOT-watching variant literally contains "NOT watching" and never claims coverage.

capabilities.name: Backgrounded coverage claim in the pump foreground notification
capabilities.behavior: `PumpConnectionService` (CHANNEL_ID "pump_connection", name "Pump Connection", IMPORTANCE_LOW, no badge; NOTIFICATION_ID = 1) mutates its ongoing, always-silent notification text from the SAME AlertFloorStatusProvider stream — while the app is closed this is the only surface that can say whether anything is watching. `onCreate` seeds `lastFloorStatus = alertFloorStatusProvider.current()` (pessimistic) so a cold start into an existing outage (post-reboot) does not render all-is-well copy; `onStartCommand` rebuilds from the CACHED status, never the default. A `floorStatusWatcherJob` collects `observe()`, refreshes `backendConfigured` per emission, stores lastFloorStatus, and re-notifies NOTIFICATION_ID 1. Text: ServerActive → "Reading pump data in background"; FloorWatching + backend → "Server alerts paused — this phone is watching for lows and highs"; FloorWatching BLE-only → "This phone is watching for lows and highs"; FloorNotWatching (any reason) → "Alerts degraded — this phone is NOT watching for lows or highs". Title always "Connected to pump". Exceptions in the watcher are caught so a status-only surface can never take down the BLE link/polling (text then freezes at the last value).
edge_cases: The foreground notification never becomes an alarm — status text only, always the silent low-importance channel.
The not-watching text does NOT carry the specific reason (unlike the in-app banner).

capabilities.name: Alerts screen (list, empty states, refresh, per-row ack)
capabilities.behavior: `AlertsScreen` → `AlertsContent`. Column: degraded banner (padding start/end 16dp, top 8dp) then the history. When backendConfigured the history is wrapped in a Material3 `PullToRefreshBox` (testTag "alerts_pull_to_refresh") bound to uiState.isLoading / onRefresh; in BLE-only mode there is NO pull affordance at all (a pull would be a dead gesture since refreshAlerts() stands down). History list: LazyColumn, horizontal padding 16dp, 12dp item spacing, keyed by serverId, 8dp spacers top and bottom. Empty state selection is a PAIR so title/subtitle cannot drift: backend → ("No alerts", "Pull down to refresh"); BLE-only → ("No alert history", "On-device alarms appear as notifications, not in this list."); shown when alerts.isEmpty() && (!isLoading || !backendConfigured) — in BLE-only mode isLoading is ignored so an orphaned in-flight flag cannot blank the screen. Alert card: severity color emergency #D32F2F, urgent #F57C00, warning #FBC02D, else #1976D2; 40dp circular Warning icon at 15% alpha; row 1 = capitalized severity + `GlucoseFormat.formatWithLabel(currentValue.toInt(), unit)`; message maxLines 3 ellipsized; footer = patientName (primary color, caregiver only) + relative timestamp; trailing Check IconButton only when !alert.acknowledged. Timestamp format: <1 min "Just now", <60 min "Xm ago", <1440 min "Xh ago", else SimpleDateFormat("MMM d, HH:mm", default locale). Snackbar host bottom-center; errors are shown once then cleared.
edge_cases: Floor alerts never appear in this list (not persisted) — hence the BLE-only empty-state subtitle explaining that on-device alarms are notifications only.
`presentation/detail/AlertHistoryScreen.kt` is a stub: it renders "Alert history coming in Story 31.6".

capabilities.name: AlertsViewModel — state, BLE-only gating, and honest error copy
capabilities.behavior: Exposes: `uiState` (isLoading, error — always user-facing copy, never a raw exception message); `alerts` = repository.observeRecentAlerts() stateIn(WhileSubscribed(5000), emptyList()); `glucoseUnit` stateIn seeded from the cached unit; `alertFloorStatus` = provider.observe() stateIn seeded with provider.current(); `backendConfigured` = authTokenStore.backendConfiguredFlow() stateIn seeded FALSE (pessimistic — only softens copy toward BLE-only phrasing for the first frame). init: cleanupOldAlerts() + refreshAlerts(). `refreshAlerts()`: FIRST awaits `authTokenStore.backendConfiguredFlow().first()` (read off the flow, not the pessimistic StateFlow seed, so a full-stack user's cold-start fetch is not dropped) and returns silently when false (GLY-146 — no "Can't reach your server" nag for a server that never existed); else isLoading=true and fetchPendingAlerts(), mapping failures: IOException → "Can't reach your server — alerts may be out of date.", else → "Couldn't refresh alerts. Try again." `acknowledgeAlert(serverId)`: calls repository.acknowledgeAlert then UNCONDITIONALLY `alertNotificationManager.markAcknowledged(serverId)` (the row is marked locally regardless of the POST); on failure, returns silently in BLE-only mode, otherwise sets error copy from the repository's own classification: IOException or non-terminal AlertAckHttpException → "Acknowledged locally — will sync when reconnected."; terminal AlertAckHttpException → "Couldn't sync this acknowledgment to the server."; anything else → "Couldn't acknowledge the alert. Try again." `clearError()` resets error.
edge_cases: A deferral (transport/transient) is deliberately NOT phrased as an error — the ack reconciles automatically.
Cached alerts remain visible while alerting is degraded (pinned by test).

capabilities.name: Caregiver alerting
capabilities.behavior: Caregiver support is entirely server-driven: `AlertResponse.patient_name` flows into `AlertEntity.patientName` and from there into (a) the notification title suffix " - <name>", (b) the notification slot key "alertType|patientName" so two patients' same-type alerts occupy DIFFERENT slots and do not replace each other, and (c) the alert card footer (primary-colored name before the timestamp). The caregiver data-gap alert type "no_data" (GLY-137) is special-cased in `formatAlertTitle`: its currentValue is only a LAST-KNOWN reading, so the title reads "<prefix>: No CGM data<suffix>" in BOTH units and the gap age / last-known value are left to the server-authored message body. "no_data" is not in LOW/HIGH_ALERT_TYPES so it routes to the AI channel (IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT, no DND bypass). There is NO client-side caregiver escalation, fan-out, or Telegram integration — onboarding copy attributes "caregiver escalation" and "Telegram delivery" to the server ("when you connect a server"), and the watch's not-watching screen states "Caregiver & AI alerts are paused — they need the backend." The on-device floor never produces caregiver alerts (patientName is always null on floor entities).
edge_cases: A no_data alert landing on the AI channel is quieter than a glucose alert — deliberate but worth noting for the port.
Caregiver alerts arrive only over the SSE stream / pending-alerts pull; nothing local produces them.

capabilities.name: Watch alert relay (phone → wrist, GLY-116)
capabilities.behavior: Inside `PumpPollingOrchestrator.processCgmReading(reading, nowMs)` (the only production caller is pollCgm; also the debug-inject seam): (1) send the CGM DataItem to the watch (raw mg/dL + trend + timestamp + display range + unit); (2) `serverAlertType = alertFloor.classify(reading.glucoseMgDl)`; `watchAlertType = SERVER_TO_WATCH_ALERT_TYPE[serverAlertType]` where the map is low_urgent→"urgent_low", low_warning→"low", high_warning→"high", high_urgent→"urgent_high" (a miss logs a warning and yields null — it may cost the relay a push, never the floor hand-off); (3) `alertable = alertFloor.isReadingAlertable(reading, nowMs)` — the SAME data-trust bound as the floor. If alertable, under `watchRelayMutex`: new type ≠ previousAlertType → sendAlert(rebuzz = true), update previousAlertType/lastAlertSentAtMs/lastAlertBuzzAtMs; same type ongoing → rebuzz = (now - lastAlertBuzzAtMs >= WRIST_ALERT_REBUZZ_MS = AlertFloor.FLOOR_COOLDOWN_MS = 30 min), and send if rebuzz OR (now - lastAlertSentAtMs >= WRIST_ALERT_REFRESH_MS = 5 * 60_000 = 5 min) — silent 5-minute refreshes keep the wrist copy's timestamp inside the 6-minute CGM STALE band so a still-live alert is never greyed as "data stale"; classification in range (serverAlertType == null) && previousAlertType != null → `clearAlert()` (keyed on the CLASSIFICATION, not on watchAlertType being null, so a mapping gap can never produce a false "All clear"). If NOT alertable the WHOLE relay block is skipped — no sendAlert, no clearAlert, latch untouched (retracting would flip a possibly-still-true low into a reassuring "All clear" off data nobody can vouch for; the watch ages it out on its own clock instead). The floor hand-off `alertFloor.onCgmReading(reading, serverAlertType, nowMs)` always runs. Wire (`WearDataContract.ALERT_PATH = "/glycemicgpt/alert"`): alert_type, alert_bg (Int mg/dL), alert_ts, alert_msg ("<URGENT LOW|LOW|HIGH|URGENT HIGH> <value+unit>"), alert_rebuzz (Bool). `clearAlert()` = sendAlert(type="none", bg=0, ts=now, message="").
edge_cases: Wrist alert paths after GLY-116 are exactly two: this relay and the BRIDGED SERVER notification. The floor notification is local-only (setLocalOnly) so a single fresh low is one wrist experience, not three.

Watch side: rebuzz=false updates the display without vibrating; the key defaults to TRUE when absent so older phone builds still buzz. Vibration: urgent* → waveform [0, 500, 200, 500]; otherwise one-shot 300 ms, default amplitude; suppressed entirely when the watch-face config `showAlert` is off. Received bg is validated `isValidGlucose` (20..500) and zeroed if invalid.

capabilities.name: Wrist coverage mirror (monitoring status) and watch alert surfaces
capabilities.behavior: `WearMonitoringStatusForwarder` (started on the pump service's scope) collects the SAME AlertFloorStatusProvider stream and pushes it to `MONITORING_STATUS_PATH = "/glycemicgpt/monitoring_status"` with keys mon_state, mon_reason, mon_timeout_ms plus a `_ts` to defeat DataLayer dedup. Wire vocabulary mirrors AlertFloorStatus exactly: "server_active", "floor_watching", "not_watching" (+ reason = the FloorNotWatchingReason ENUM NAME verbatim: NOTIFICATIONS_DENIED / THRESHOLDS_NOT_SYNCED / THRESHOLDS_NOT_CONFIGURED / PUMP_DISCONNECTED / NO_FRESH_READING). Advertised timeout = `FreshnessPolicy.cgm(fast).staleAfterMs` (6 min real, 20 s debug). Re-send cadence = heartbeat as well as on change: `heartbeatPeriodMs(timeout) = max(timeout / 2, MIN_HEARTBEAT_MS = 5_000)` → 3 min real, 10 s debug — because the provider deduplicates, a healthy steady state would otherwise emit once and a watch that then lost the phone would hold a frozen "watching" forever. retryWhen with RETRY_DELAY_MS = 5_000. Watch side: the timeout is clamped into [MIN_STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000, MAX_STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS = 30 * 60_000] and unknown state strings are REJECTED; status is stored with the watch-clock receivedAtMs and is deliberately NOT persisted (after a watch process restart coverage is genuinely unknown). `WatchDataRepository.coverageFrom(status, nowMs)` → WristCoverage: null status → NoRecentStatus; age < -STATUS_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS (60 s) or age >= timeoutMs → NoRecentStatus; server_active/floor_watching → Watching; not_watching → NotWatching(reason); unknown → NoRecentStatus (fail closed everywhere). Watch Alerts screen re-evaluates on a 15 s ticker: with no alert it shows "No Active Alert"/"All clear" (green #4ADE80) ONLY while Watching; NotWatching shows "Not watching" + per-reason copy + "Caregiver & AI alerts are paused — they need the backend."; NoRecentStatus shows "No recent data" + "The watch hasn't heard from your phone recently. Alerts may not arrive." With an alert showing, its age is computed on the WATCH clock and once `WatchFreshness.cgmTier` is TOO_STALE the alert greys (#9CA3AF) and the age line reads "as of Xm ago — data stale"; if additionally not covered, an extra amber "Not watching — check your phone" line appears. Dismiss button sends ALERT_DISMISS_PATH and clears the local alert. Alerts complication (SmallImage bell): tint DEFAULT grey / WARNING amber #FBBF24 / URGENT red #EF4444 by the rules: stale alert + covered → grey; stale alert + not covered → amber; urgent → red; any active alert → amber; not covered → amber; else grey — the stale-alert grey is only allowed while something is watching, otherwise a dead phone behind a stale alert would look like a healthy all-clear.
edge_cases: The watch NEVER re-derives coverage — it renders the phone's decision and decays it locally. Silence longer than the advertised window is the phone-death signal.
Pre-GLY-116 phone builds omitting the timeout key fall back to DEFAULT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS = CGM_STALE_AFTER_MS = 6 min.

capabilities.name: Watch-initiated dismiss → phone acknowledge
capabilities.behavior: `WearChatRelayService` (WearableListenerService) handles MessageClient path ALERT_DISMISS_PATH = "/glycemicgpt/alert/dismiss": promotes itself to foreground work, then `runBlocking { serverId = alertRepository.getLatestUnacknowledgedServerId(); if (serverId != null) alertRepository.acknowledgeAlert(serverId) ...; wearDataSender.clearAlert() }`. Because acknowledgeAlert marks the Room row locally BEFORE the server POST, the watch's clearAlert is truthful even when the backend is unreachable — the alert cannot re-fire and the server sync is deferred to the reconcile. `getLatestUnacknowledgedServerId()` = `SELECT server_id FROM alerts WHERE acknowledged = 0 ORDER BY timestamp_ms DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1`.
edge_cases: A wrist dismiss acknowledges the NEWEST unacknowledged SERVER alert — it has no way to target a specific alert, and it can never acknowledge a floor alert (floor alerts are not in Room), so a floor alarm on the phone is not silenced by a wrist dismiss.
With no unacknowledged server alert, only the wrist copy is cleared.

capabilities.name: Notification permission handling and the floor's dependency on it
capabilities.behavior: `canPostAlertNotifications()` = `NotificationManagerCompat.from(context).areNotificationsEnabled()` — deliberately chosen over a raw POST_NOTIFICATIONS check because it also covers the app-level notifications toggle in system settings on pre-Tiramisu OSes (minSdk 30). It gates: the floor's gate 4, the head of showAlertNotification, and the status selector's NOTIFICATIONS_DENIED reason (the highest-priority reason, because it is durable and user-fixable). Onboarding requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS on both paths (after login and on `continueWithoutServer()`), explicitly documented as safety-critical: without it the alert floor is silently suppressed and a tier-1 user could believe they are monitored when they are not. Settings → Notifications → `NotificationPermissionSection` re-checks on every ON_RESUME and offers a button that opens `Settings.ACTION_APP_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS` for the package (falls back to a Toast if the activity is missing).
edge_cases: The floor checks permission BEFORE stamping the cooldown so a permission granted moments later still gets its alarm (pinned by test).

capabilities.name: Debug fault injection for alerting
capabilities.behavior: Two debug-only toggles (both hard-gated on BuildConfig.DEBUG in the getter, so they are always false in release). (1) "Simulate backend unreachable" (pref key debug_simulate_backend_unreachable): `SimulateUnreachableInterceptor` throws IOException before the network on every request through it, on the main client AND the SSE client (the SSE client would otherwise reconnect successfully and never sit in RECONNECTING, leaving the alert-floor arm-condition only half-drivable in E2E); AlertStreamService additionally force-cancels the live eventSource when the toggle flips on so the fault takes effect immediately instead of after the 75 s read timeout. On the main client the interceptor sits BELOW ReachabilityInterceptor so the injected failure is recorded exactly like a real transport failure (2 consecutive failures flip NetworkStatus to BACKEND_UNREACHABLE). (2) "Fast staleness" (pref key debug_fast_staleness): swaps FreshnessPolicy.CGM for CGM_DEBUG_FAST (20 s / 45 s) in the floor gate, the status pipeline, the provider's tick cadence, and the wrist status timeout, so FRESH→STALE→TOO_STALE transitions can be observed in seconds. Both expose `...Flow()` callbackFlows so consumers react immediately.
edge_cases: NetworkMonitor.FAILURE_THRESHOLD = 2 consecutive transport failures before BACKEND_UNREACHABLE; any HTTP response (even 4xx/5xx) counts as reachable; device-offline takes precedence and reports OFFLINE. There is intentionally NO backend health endpoint.

capabilities.name: Alerting lifecycle across app/device restarts
capabilities.behavior: AlertStreamService is started from: (a) `AuthRepository.login()` on success; (b) `SettingsViewModel` init when logged in; (c) `BootCompletedReceiver` on ACTION_BOOT_COMPLETED / QUICKBOOT_POWERON when `authTokenStore.getRefreshToken() != null` (wrapped in try/catch for ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException and SecurityException, using goAsync() to extend the broadcast window past the 10 s ANR limit). It is stopped from `AuthRepository.logout()` and self-stops when a scheduled reconnect finds no active session. PumpConnectionService (which hosts the floor status watcher and the wrist forwarder) is started from `GlycemicGptApp.onCreate` when a pump is paired, and from BootCompletedReceiver when paired. `GlycemicGptApp.onCreate` also plants Timber, inits Sentry, starts NetworkMonitor, and installs the app-lifetime REACHABLE→reconcilePendingAcks collector.
edge_cases: No FCM/push path exists: `DeviceRegistrationRequest.device_token` is a locally generated random UUID persisted in AppSettingsStore, not a push token — alert delivery is 100% SSE + on-device floor.

safety_critical: NEVER FIRE ON A NON-FRESH READING (AlertFloor). The floor may alarm only when isFreshForAlertFloor(age, activePolicy) is true — strictly FRESH (< 6 min for CGM, < 20 s under the debug policy); STALE and TOO_STALE both suppress. Age is computed against the CGM's OWN sensor timestamp, never poll wall-clock, because a warmup/signal-loss poll can succeed every 15 s while returning the same stale sensor value.

Wall-clock rewind guard: a BACKWARD clock jump shrinks a stale reading's apparent age and would resurrect it. AlertFloor keeps a monotonic high-water mark of every observed wall-clock time; while now + 60_000 ms < highWater, evaluation is suppressed AND the surface reports NOT watching. Residual (accepted, documented): a rewind while the process is not running leaves no mark and can under-age a stale reading — fails toward alarming, never toward silence.

Forward clock-skew tolerance: ALERT_FLOOR_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS = 60_000. Readings future-dated by up to 60 s still alarm (pump clocks drift); beyond that they are rejected. A hard age >= 0 gate would silently disable the floor for any user with a slightly fast pump clock — the same lethal failure inverted.

Never alarm off unconfigured thresholds: AlertThresholdStore.isConfigured() (source != NONE) gates the floor. The defaults 55/70/180/250 exist only for the watch relay's classifier and were chosen by no user.

Glucose-validity bound 20..500 mg/dL is enforced on every threshold write (updateAll/updateLocal require(), the Settings editor, and the backend-sync validator) and on the watch's received alert bg value. Out-of-range input persists NOTHING and throws / surfaces an inline error — never clamps.

Threshold ordering invariant urgentLow <= lowWarning < highWarning <= urgentHigh (store + editor). The backend sync validates ordering on the RAW FLOATS with all-strict comparisons before rounding, because rounding two server-legal values <1 mg/dL apart could collapse them and permanently disarm the floor. An invalid server response is DROPPED, never clamped, leaving last-known-good values.

Unit conversion: MGDL_PER_MMOL = 18.0156 is the single canonical constant (mirrors backend src/core/units.py and the web). Storage, alert detection, thresholds, and all wire values stay canonical mg/dL; mmol/L is display-only, converted ONCE and rounded LAST. The Settings editor parses mmol input back to mg/dL via *18.0156 roundToInt, and quotes mmol bounds that themselves round back inside 20..500. A drift here desyncs the client from the server (docs/contract/safety-constants.md, enforced by SafetyConstantDriftGuardTest).

Channel routing by alert type: a drifted low_* string would route a life-threatening low off the IMPORTANCE_HIGH, bypassDnd, USAGE_ALARM channel onto the IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT AI channel — a silent safety downgrade. LOW/HIGH_ALERT_TYPES live in one shared object for exactly this reason.

Alert delivery guarantee on acknowledge (GLY-130): the local Room mark runs FIRST and every local silence op (cancel notification, restore alarm volume, clear dedup id) runs BEFORE and INDEPENDENTLY of the server POST. An unreachable or hung backend can never leave the alarm sounding. Order is pinned by coVerifyOrder tests.

Ack clobber guard: AlertDao.insertPreservingLocalAck never downgrades a locally-acknowledged row from a stale server echo; AlertStreamService branches on the RETURNED entity's acknowledged, so an SSE re-delivery cannot re-alarm an alert the user already acknowledged offline.

Bounded snooze, never permanent silence: an acked, never-recovering low re-alarms exactly FLOOR_COOLDOWN_MS (30 min) after the ack, and a recovery + re-cross alarms immediately as a distinct episode. Deliberate divergence from the server (which would re-alert every evaluation cycle) to avoid alarm-spam that trains users to disable notifications.

Episode-guard failure mode is fail-open toward alerting: a DB exception in getLatestUnacknowledgedTimestampForType is caught and treated as "no recent server alert", so a broken lookup may cost one duplicate alarm, never a missed one. The server-alert seed is clamped to min(serverTs, now) so clock skew cannot stretch the 30-minute silence window.

Honest coverage claim (the "lethal lie"): the UI must never say "watching" when the floor cannot fire. alertFloorStatus mirrors every firing gate plus pumpConnected, the pipeline recomputes on a ticker so the claim DECAYS to NOT watching on its own, retryWhen emits a pessimistic snapshot rather than freezing, and current() seeds pessimistically (no CGM age, backendConfigured=false).

Staleness detection is one definition in one place: isReadingAlertable is shared by the floor and the watch relay; a second staleness definition on either path is the exact silent-floor bug the design exists to prevent (guarded by AlertRelayFloorDivergenceTest and AlertFloorArmingConsistencyTest).

Wrist honesty: a not-alertable reading skips the WHOLE relay block — never a clearAlert, because retracting a possibly-still-true low into "All clear" off untrustworthy data is the opposite lie. clearAlert is keyed on the classification being in range, never on a mapping-gap null. The watch fails closed on missing/aged/unknown status and on a backward watch-clock jump.
no_data (caregiver data-gap) alerts must never render their currentValue in the title — it is a LAST-KNOWN reading and would fake a live glucose during exactly the blackout being reported.

Notification permission is a coverage precondition: a floor that cannot post is not watching. It is checked before the cooldown is stamped, is the highest-priority NOT-watching reason, and is requested during onboarding on both the server and BLE-only paths.

Logout/BLE-only transitions disarm BACKEND thresholds (so the floor can never fire off another account's levels) while preserving LOCAL device-set thresholds (so a user is not silently disarmed with nothing to restore from).

Floor notifications are local-only on the wrist (setLocalOnly) while SERVER notifications must keep bridging — server alerts fire off a different (cloud) glucose source and are the only wrist path left while the pump CGM is stale.

Architectural shape worth carrying to Swift: there are exactly TWO alert sources — the backend (delivered over a single SSE stream, plus a pending-alerts pull) and the on-device alert floor (threshold-only, gated on data trust). They are mutually exclusive by construction: gate 1 of the floor is `isAlertingDegraded`, so while the server can deliver, the floor is silent. The three coverage surfaces (in-app banner, pump foreground-notification text, wrist status) all read the SAME `AlertFloorStatusProvider` stream so they can never disagree; do not fork that pipeline in the port.

Numbers a Swift engineer needs (all exact, all from source): SSE connectTimeout 30 s, readTimeout 75 s, server heartbeat ~30 s, STABLE_CONNECTION_MS 10 s, backoff `min(1000 * 2^min(attempt,6), 60_000)`, 401/403 jumps attempt to max(5, attempt). FLOOR_COOLDOWN_MS 1_800_000 (30 min), mirrored by WRIST_ALERT_REBUZZ_MS; WRIST_ALERT_REFRESH_MS 300_000 (5 min). Foreground notification IDs: 1 = pump, 2 = alert stream; alert slot IDs coerced >= 100. Terminal ack codes {403, 404, 422}. NetworkMonitor FAILURE_THRESHOLD 2. MGDL_PER_MMOL 18.0156.

Explicit "we deliberately did NOT do X" decisions found in source (all load-bearing):
- The floor is threshold-only: NO trajectory projection, NO prediction horizons, NO IoB escalation — those stay server-side, and the notification body says so verbatim.
- The floor does NOT re-alarm an acked sustained low on every 15 s poll the way the server does; it waits one full 30-minute cooldown. Justified as anti-alarm-fatigue.
- Unacknowledged cooldowns deliberately do NOT re-arm on recovery (only acked types do) — boundary flapping of a hovering glucose must not re-alarm while the notification is still up.
- There is intentionally NO backend health endpoint; reachability is inferred client-side from existing traffic.
- There is NO push/FCM path at all; `device_token` is a locally generated UUID for server-side device bookkeeping.
- Floor alerts are NEVER persisted to the alerts table (server history only) and their synthetic `local-floor:` id must never reach the acknowledge endpoint.
- Floor notifications are deliberately local-only on the wrist; server notifications deliberately keep bridging.
- The alerting-degraded predicate is deliberately pessimistic on disagreement between NetworkStatus and stream state.
- `AlertFloorStatusProvider.current()` deliberately seeds backendConfigured=false and cgmAge=null rather than doing a synchronous encrypted-store read on the main thread; it may under-claim but never over-claim.

Gaps / bugs found while reading (report as-is, not editorializing about iOS):
1. `AlertNotificationManager` puts `navigate_to = "alerts"` on the content intent, but `MainActivity` reads no intent extras at all (the manifest carries an explicit comment that no incoming intent data/extras are processed). Tapping an alert notification therefore just opens the app at its default destination — deep-link-to-Alerts is NOT implemented.
2. `AlertStreamService.connectToStream()` increments `connectionGeneration` twice per connect (once before cancelling the previous source at line ~195, once when capturing `gen` at line ~213). Harmless today because both happen before the listener is attached, but do not port it as if the double bump were meaningful.
